units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Must you really?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Kisses her .
Yes.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Then do tell her I want to talk to her particularly. I have been waiting here all the morning to see either her or Robert.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Do you mean to say you didn’t come here expressly to propose to me?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Triumphantly .
No; that was a flash of genius.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Your first.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: With determination .
My last.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I am delighted to hear it. Now don’t stir. I’ll be back in five minutes. And don’t fall into any temptations while I am away.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Dear Mabel, while you are away, there are none. It makes me horribly dependent on you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter LADY CHILTERN.
Good morning, dear! How pretty you are looking!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: How pale you are looking, Gertrude! It is most becoming!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Good morning, Lord Goring!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Bowing .
Good morning, Lady Chiltern!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Aside to LORD GORING.
I shall be in the conservatory under the second palm tree on the left.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Second on the left?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: With a look of mock surprise .
Yes; the usual palm tree.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Blows a kiss to him , unobserved by LADY CHILTERN, and goes out .
Lady Chiltern, I have a certain amount of very good news to tell you. Mrs. Cheveley gave me up Robert’s letter last night, and I burned it. Robert is safe.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Sinking on the sofa .
Safe! Oh! I am so glad of that. What a good friend you are to him—to us!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: There is only one person now that could be said to be in any danger.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Who is that?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Sitting down beside her .
Yourself.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I? In danger? What do you mean?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Danger is too great a word. It is a word I should not have used. But I admit I have something to tell you that may distress you, that terribly distresses me. Yesterday evening you wrote me a very beautiful, womanly letter, asking me for my help. You wrote to me as one of your oldest friends, one of your husband’s oldest friends. Mrs. Cheveley stole that letter from my rooms.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, what use is it to her? Why should she not have it?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Rising .
Lady Chiltern, I will be quite frank with you. Mrs. Cheveley puts a certain construction on that letter and proposes to send it to your husband.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: But what construction could she put on it? . . . Oh! not that! not that! If I in—in trouble, and wanting your help, trusting you, propose to come to you . . . that you may advise me . . . assist me . . . Oh! are there women so horrible as that . . .? And she proposes to send it to my husband? Tell me what happened. Tell me all that happened.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Mrs. Cheveley was concealed in a room adjoining my library, without my knowledge. I thought that the person who was waiting in that room to see me was yourself. Robert came in unexpectedly. A chair or something fell in the room. He forced his way in, and he discovered her. We had a terrible scene. I still thought it was you. He left me in anger. At the end of everything Mrs. Cheveley got possession of your letter—she stole it, when or how, I don’t know.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: At what hour did this happen?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: At half-past ten. And now I propose that we tell Robert the whole thing at once.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Looking at him with amazement that is almost terror .

You want me to tell Robert that the woman you expected was not Mrs. Cheveley, but myself? That it was I whom you thought was concealed in a room in your house, at half-past ten o’clock at night? You want me to tell him that?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: I think it is better that he should know the exact truth.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rising .
Oh, I couldn’t, I couldn’t!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN
